title: A Systematic Review of ChatGPT for English as a Foreign Language Writing: Opportunities, Challenges, and Recommendations
extended_summary:
This paper asks how ChatGPT is being used in English as a Foreign Language (EFL) writing and what opportunities, challenges, and recommendations emerge from the existing literature. Rather than reporting a new classroom intervention, it systematically reviews 20 of the most relevant empirical studies on ChatGPT and EFL writing published in 2023–2024, following PRISMA guidelines. The review draws on studies of learner perceptions, writing improvement, automated feedback, automated essay scoring, and teacher feedback support.

Across the reviewed literature, ChatGPT is portrayed as a tool that can support multiple stages of writing, including brainstorming, outlining, drafting, revising, proofreading, summarizing, and reflective comparison of AI output with human knowledge. The paper emphasizes that ChatGPT can provide instant feedback, generate prompts, and sometimes approximate human scoring or error detection, but it is weaker on deep structure, pragmatics, and context-sensitive judgment. Several studies also suggest that ChatGPT may improve learner motivation, self-efficacy, and teacher self-efficacy when integrated into instruction.

The paper focuses on EFL learners and teachers in a range of international contexts, especially studies from East Asia, and argues for a balanced, supervised, and collaborative approach to AI integration. The author concludes that ChatGPT should complement rather than replace human instruction, with teacher oversight, critical engagement, and AI literacy practices built into writing curricula. The recommendations stress ethical use, collaboration between teachers and learners, and deliberate alignment between ChatGPT use and writing pedagogy.
quality_tier_rationale: This is a systematic review, but it synthesizes heterogeneous primary studies rather than presenting a single well-controlled causal design. The evidence base includes a mix of experimental, correlational, and descriptive studies, so credibility is informative but not high enough for blue/green on the review alone.
impact_tier_rationale: The reviewed studies suggest meaningful promise for writing improvement and motivation, but the paper does not report pooled effect sizes and repeatedly notes limitations and context dependence. Overall impact appears promising but still modest/unclear at the review level rather than definitively large.

interventions.use_case: Systematic review of ChatGPT use in EFL writing for brainstorming, drafting, editing, proofreading, feedback generation, register awareness, and writing assessment support.
ChatGPT used as an automated writing evaluation and feedback tool to identify errors, provide corrective feedback, and compare with human teacher feedback.
ChatGPT used as a conversational writing assistant/mentor that answers questions, supports prompt-based writing tasks, and scaffolds planning and revision.

finding.finding_summary: Across the reviewed studies, ChatGPT generally improved EFL writing quality, especially organization, coherence, grammar, vocabulary, clarity, and cohesion. Evidence included significant gains in writing skills in several intervention studies (e.g., Song & Song, 2023; Yan, 2023; Ghafouri et al., 2024), but the review also noted limitations in detecting deep-structure and pragmatic errors and uneven effectiveness across registers.
finding.measure: EFL academic writing performance, writing skill ratings, error detection, coherence/clarity, register knowledge, automated essay scoring, revised essay scores
finding.study_size: various studies reviewed; not_reported for aggregate synthesis

finding.finding_summary: The review reports improved writing motivation, self-efficacy, engagement, and behavioral intention to use ChatGPT among EFL learners. For example, studies summarized in the review found significant gains in motivation and self-efficacy after AI-assisted instruction, and positive attitudes toward continued use.
finding.measure: Motivation surveys, self-efficacy scales, attitudes, behavioral intention, engagement reports
finding.study_size: various studies reviewed; not_reported for aggregate synthesis

finding.finding_summary: ChatGPT was framed as supporting critical thinking and collaborative writing, but the review also warned that over-reliance could weaken critical thinking and independent writing development. Students were reported to engage in collaborative writing and reflective comparison tasks, yet the paper emphasized the need for corroboration, critical evaluation, and human oversight.
finding.measure: Collaborative writing tendency, reflective comparison tasks, critical engagement with AI output, reported dependence/over-reliance concerns
finding.study_size: various studies reviewed; not_reported for aggregate synthesis

finding.finding_summary: The review consistently describes ChatGPT as improving writing efficiency through rapid feedback, automated drafting support, brainstorming, summarization, and scalable scoring. It was repeatedly characterized as reducing teacher workload and speeding up editing/proofreading, although the paper does not report a pooled effect size.
finding.measure: Feedback turnaround, writing efficiency, teacher workload, scalability of assessment, automated workflow support
finding.study_size: various studies reviewed; not_reported for aggregate synthesis

finding.finding_summary: The paper argues that ChatGPT may reshape writing curricula, teacher roles, and AI literacy practices, but it also highlights governance concerns such as academic integrity, privacy, and unequal access. Recommendations emphasize curriculum integration, teacher-student communities of practice, and supervised implementation rather than unfettered adoption.
finding.measure: Curriculum recommendations, academic integrity concerns, privacy/ethics considerations, institutional guidance
